title: Supernetting and summarisation
summary: Combine many routes into one, and know when a summary lies.

steps.title: One route instead of four
body: A router that knows `192.168.0.0/24`, `.1.0/24`, `.2.0/24` and `.3.0/24` behind the same next hop can advertise **one** route: `192.168.0.0/22`.
This is **summarisation** (or **supernetting**). It keeps routing tables small and hides churn inside a site.
The summary keeps the **common leading bits** of the first and last address:
Step through the program: it shortens the prefix until both ends agree.

steps.prompt: Same program for `10.1.4.0` to `10.1.7.255`. What does it print?
steps.explain: 4 = 000001|00 and 7 = 000001|11: the first 6 bits of the third octet agree, so 16 + 6 = 22.
4 and 5 differ only in the last bit of the third octet, so one bit less than /24.

steps.prompt: Match each set of routes to its tightest summary.
A branch owns only `10.1.1.0/24` and `10.1.2.0/24`, and advertises `10.1.0.0/22`. What's the risk?
options: It also claims 10.1.0.0/24 and 10.1.3.0/24, attracting traffic it will drop (a black hole)
steps.explain: 1 and 2 aren't aligned on a /23, so the only covering summary is a /22 that includes addresses the branch doesn't have.

code: 16 = 0001|0000 and 31 = 0001|1111 share __1__ bits of the third octet, so the summary is 192.168.16.0/__2__

steps.title: Summarise routes
prompt: Write `string Summary(List<string> cidrs)` returning the smallest single CIDR covering every block: find the lowest network and highest broadcast,
then shorten the prefix until both agree. Helpers are given.
starter: uint ToUInt(string ip) => ip.Split('.').Aggregate(0u, (acc, o) => (acc << 8) | uint.Parse(o));
uint MaskOf(int prefix) => prefix == 0 ? 0u : uint.MaxValue << (32 - prefix);
solution: uint ToUInt(string ip) => ip.Split('.').Aggregate(0u, (acc, o) => (acc << 8) | uint.Parse(o));
uint MaskOf(int prefix) => prefix == 0 ? 0u : uint.MaxValue << (32 - prefix);

steps.title: Is the summary exact?
prompt: Write `bool IsExact(List<string> cidrs)` (non-overlapping blocks assumed): true when the summary from your `Summary` covers **only** these blocks,
i.e. its size equals the sum of their sizes. Paste `Summary` too.
starter: uint ToUInt(string ip) => ip.Split('.').Aggregate(0u, (acc, o) => (acc << 8) | uint.Parse(o));
uint MaskOf(int prefix) => prefix == 0 ? 0u : uint.MaxValue << (32 - prefix);
solution: uint ToUInt(string ip) => ip.Split('.').Aggregate(0u, (acc, o) => (acc << 8) | uint.Parse(o));
uint MaskOf(int prefix) => prefix == 0 ? 0u : uint.MaxValue << (32 - prefix);
template: Dojo.Eq("unaligned pair is not", false, IsExact(new List<string> { "10.1.1.0/24", "10.1.2.0/24" }));
hints: Compare the summary's size with the total.
